what: explicit independent sets of the level-one finite Euclidean planes UD(F_p, 2): the points (a, b) of F_p^2, adjacent when the squared difference sums to 1. A point is written both as the pair [a, b] and as the index a*p + b (the numbering of plans/FS66-phase2-certificate.md SECTION G); tools/fs66_b1_sets_check.py refuses the file if the two disagree.
licenses: the LOWER halves of the brackets in plans/FS66-phase2-certificate.md SECTION ST, and nothing else. Reduction modulo p is a graph homomorphism UD(Z/p^k, 2) -> UD(F_p, 2), so the full preimage of an independent set is independent: alpha(UD(Z/p^k, 2)) >= alpha(UD(F_p, 2)) * p^(2(k-1)). With the certificates cert-p7.json and cert-p11.json for the upper halves: alpha(UD(Z/49, 2)) = 686 EXACTLY (14*49 = 686 = floor(14.015224*49)), and 3388 <= alpha(UD(Z/121, 2)) <= 3412 (28*121 = 3388, floor(28.204320*121) = 3412). Also chi_f(UD(Z/p^k, 2)) <= p^2/alpha(UD(F_p, 2)) at every level: <= 3.5 at 7, <= 4.3215 at 11. Only alpha(UD(F_p, 2)) >= size is used here, never equality -- the sets happen to be maximum (FS-54, a different instrument), and no claim here rests on that.

provenance.found_by: p = 7: a union of two cosets of an additive F_7-line avoiding the unit circle. p = 11: randomised greedy plus (1,2)-swap local search, seed 20260921. How they were found is not on the trust surface: the only property used is the one tools/fs66_b1_sets_check.py tests from the definition.
